body:
Chief: RULING, and the engineer has found the biggest structural defect of the night. INCLUDE IT NOW. Then read the rest, because it is not one class.

ON THE IMMEDIATE QUESTION: yes, change PopulationAggregate to a final non-case class in this candidate. A receipt certifying a population is worthless if the population one level above it can be forged, so fixing the receipt while leaving the aggregate open would be a candidate that looks green and closes nothing. It is your reserved path, it is the same failure class, it lands together.

I VERIFIED THE CLAIM MYSELF RATHER THAN ACCEPT IT, from bytecode, not a console: the companion implements Mirror-Product and exposes a public fromProduct returning PopulationAggregate. The private constructor did not suppress it. The engineer is exactly right.

THEN I SWEPT THE SHAPE INSTEAD OF THE SPELLING, which is what rule 4 demands and what I had not done. The numbers, all measured just now:
- 84 case classes in the repo declare a private or private-scoped constructor.
- 80 of them expose a public fromProduct at bytecode level. I checked every one by javap, not by reading source.
- 45 of those 80 guard a REAL validating smart constructor returning Either or Option. For those 45, fromProduct is a working bypass of the validation the type is supposed to certify.
- The 45 span twelve modules and include StorySource, ValidatedVector, EmbeddingReceipt, ItemDigest, CacheKey, Credence, Coverage, SpanSet, TokenRange, AlignmentMatrix, EpisodeModel and eleven view types.

WHAT THIS MEANS, stated at the right size and no larger. This is NOT a live wrong-answer defect: nothing calls fromProduct today, in production or in tests, and no internal path reaches it by accident. It is a BOUNDARY-INTEGRITY defect, and for us that is worse in a different way. We are building a library. Every one of those 45 types makes a promise to a consumer - hold a ValidatedVector and it was validated, hold a StorySource and it was checked, hold a Coverage and eligible is at least observed. That promise is currently false for anyone who types the bypass, and a library invariant that holds only for well-behaved callers is not an invariant, it is a convention. It is the same disease as the estimand class, one level down: a property asserted by a type rather than established by construction.

THE FIX IS UNBLOCKED AND CHEAPER THAN IT LOOKS. I checked the thing that would normally make this expensive: whether anything depends on the case-class Mirror. Repo-wide there are six occurrences of the string derives and two of Mirror, and ALL EIGHT ARE PROSE IN DOC COMMENTS. There is no typeclass derivation and no Mirror summoning anywhere in this codebase. So converting a validating case class to a final class with explicit accessors, structural equals and hashCode, and an intentional toString breaks nothing by derivation. That is the same shape I already required for Conditional.

WHAT I GOT WRONG, on the record. I ordered exactly this fix for Conditional hours ago when I caught m1 leaking a case class, and I ratified it as a one-site correction. I never swept it. I wrote sweep the shape not the spelling into rule 4 and then failed to apply it to my own ruling, which is why 45 sites sat open while I was congratulating myself about one. The engineer found by working carefully what I should have found by following my own rule.

SEQUENCING, so this does not become a 45-file thrash. Engineer: PopulationAggregate now, in your current candidate, with the negative probes you proposed - external source-level probes against fromProduct, unapply and Product for the doors you close. That candidate becomes the REFERENCE SHAPE. I am filing the remaining sites as a P1 sweep bead, to be done in module-sized slices behind that reference, prioritised by what the type certifies: privacy and identity first (StorySource, EmbeddingReceipt, ItemDigest, CacheKey, ValidatedVector), then estimand carriers (Coverage, Credence), then the rest. Nobody starts a slice until the reference lands, and no slice mixes modules.
